21.summary: Cleartext file transfer service. Primary objectives: check anonymous login, inspect server banner for known backdoors, search for sensitive/backup files, and test weak credentials.

steps.title: Check Anonymous Login
steps.desc: Many FTP servers accidentally permit anonymous login with empty or arbitrary passwords, exposing sensitive files.
steps.indicator: Look for '230 Login successful' or file directory listings.

steps.title: Banner Grabbing & Known Backdoors
steps.desc: Identify exact FTP software version (e.g. vsftpd 2.3.4 contains a backdoor smiley ':)' trigger; ProFTPD 1.3.3c contains a backdoor).
steps.indicator: Inspect greeting for vsftpd 2.3.4, ProFTPD 1.3.5 mod_copy, or pure-ftpd.

steps.title: Brute Force Default / Weak Credentials
steps.desc: Check for common admin/service credentials like admin:admin, ftp:ftp, or test wordlists.
steps.termux_cmd: hydra -l ftp -P /sdcard/passwords.txt ftp://<target>:<port> || python3 -m pip install ftplib
steps.indicator: Hydra reports valid login credentials [230 User logged in].

steps.title: Download and Inspect Directory Contents
steps.desc: Recursively download accessible files to search for SSH keys, database backups, source code, and .env files.
steps.indicator: Look for .sql, .bak, config.php, id_rsa, and credentials.

22.summary: Encrypted remote administration terminal. Primary objectives: fingerprint OpenSSH version (check CVEs), test allowed authentication methods (password vs key), test default accounts, and check for weak keys.

steps.title: Grab SSH Version & Check CVEs
steps.desc: Extract OpenSSH banner to check for known vulnerabilities like regreSSHion (CVE-2024-6387 RCE in glibc-based systems) or Terrapin (CVE-2023-48795).
steps.indicator: Review banner (e.g. 'SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.2p1'). OpenSSH 8.5p1 to 9.7p1 are vulnerable to regreSSHion.

steps.title: Enumerate Supported Authentication Methods
steps.desc: Determine if the server accepts password authentication or strictly enforces public key authentication.
steps.kali_cmd: ssh -v -o PreferredAuthentications=none -p <port> user@<target> 2>&1 | grep 'Authentications that can continue'
steps.indicator: If 'password' is listed, credential brute forcing is possible.

steps.title: Test Default / Common Credentials
steps.desc: Test common administrative and hardware accounts (e.g. root:root, admin:admin, pi:raspberry, ubuntu:ubuntu).
steps.indicator: Valid login discovered by Hydra.

steps.title: Audit Ciphers and Key Exchange Algorithms
steps.desc: Scan for obsolete/deprecated ciphers such as 3DES, CBC mode ciphers, and weak MD5/SHA1 MACs.
steps.indicator: Presence of 'arcfour', 'blowfish', or '3des-cbc'.

23.summary: Legacy unencrypted interactive text protocol. All traffic is sent in cleartext without encryption. Primary objectives: check banner, test default device passwords, and sniff traffic if on LAN.

steps.title: Connect and Inspect Login Banner
steps.desc: Connect to inspect the operating system, router make/model, and login prompt.
steps.indicator: Exposes router model (e.g. Cisco, MikroTik, BusyBox, Huawei).

steps.title: Test Vendor Default Router / IoT Credentials
steps.desc: Test factory default combinations (admin:admin, root:root, admin:password, cisco:cisco, root:toor).
steps.indicator: Direct shell prompt (e.g. '# ', '$ ', 'Router>') obtained.

steps.title: Network Sniffing Alert (If Local Subnet / Wi-Fi)
steps.desc: Because Telnet transmits passwords in cleartext, any attacker on the local network or Wi-Fi can capture credentials.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Telnet sends plaintext credentials across the wire; capture with tshark/tcpdump.'
steps.indicator: Cleartext username and password strings visible in packet payload.

25.summary: Mail delivery agent. Primary objectives: check for open relay (spam exploitation), enumerate valid local user mailboxes via VRFY/EXPN, and test STARTTLS encryption.

steps.title: Test for Open Mail Relay
steps.desc: An open relay permits unauthorized third parties to route spam and phishing emails through the server.
steps.indicator: Nmap script reports 'Server is an open relay'.

steps.title: Enumerate System Accounts (VRFY / EXPN / RCPT TO)
steps.desc: Many mail servers leak valid operating system user accounts through VRFY or RCPT TO commands.
steps.indicator: Server responds with '250 User exists' or '252 Cannot verify'.

steps.title: Verify STARTTLS Configuration
steps.desc: Ensure the mail transport is protected against passive interception by testing STARTTLS support.
steps.indicator: Inspect SSL/TLS certificate subject, issuer, and cipher suite.

53.summary: Name resolution protocol. Primary objectives: test for unauthorized DNS zone transfer (AXFR), test for open recursive resolver (DDoS amplification), and brute force subdomains.

steps.title: Attempt Full Zone Transfer (AXFR)
steps.desc: A misconfigured DNS server allows full zone transfers, leaking all internal hostnames, subdomains, and IP mappings.
steps.indicator: Outputs full list of A, CNAME, MX, and TXT records.

steps.title: Check for Open Recursive Resolver
steps.desc: Open resolvers can be abused in DNS amplification DDoS attacks.
steps.indicator: Query responds with answers to non-authoritative external domains.

steps.title: Enumerate Subdomains via Wordlist
steps.desc: Brute force common hostnames (dev, api, admin, vpn, mail, internal, test).
steps.termux_cmd: for s in www mail dev test api vpn; do dig @<target> $s.<target_domain> +short; done
steps.indicator: Resolves previously hidden internal server IPs.

80.summary: Unencrypted web application traffic. Primary objectives: technology fingerprinting, directory and endpoint discovery, security headers check, vulnerability scan, and web application attack analysis.

steps.title: Fingerprint Technologies & CMS
steps.desc: Identify web server (Apache, Nginx, IIS), backend languages (PHP, Node, Python), and CMS (WordPress, Joomla, Drupal).
steps.indicator: Look at 'Server', 'X-Powered-By', cookies, and HTML comments.

steps.title: Discover Hidden Directories & Files (Fuzzing)
steps.desc: Enumerate unlinked admin portals, backup files (.bak, .sql), environment configs (.env), and API routes.
steps.indicator: HTTP 200/301 responses on /admin, /api, /backup, /.env, /phpmyadmin.

steps.title: Inspect Sensitive Informational Files
steps.desc: Directly check for common files that disclose sensitive system details.
steps.indicator: Disallowed paths in robots.txt or 'ref: refs/heads/main' in /.git/HEAD (source code exposure).

steps.title: Run Automated Web Vulnerability Scan
steps.desc: Scan for outdated server software, default files, and dangerous HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE).
steps.indicator: Identifies CVEs, directory indexing, and missing security headers.

steps.title: Test Web Application Vulnerabilities
steps.desc: Inspect user inputs and parameters for SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and Local File Inclusion (LFI).
steps.indicator: Root entries from /etc/passwd or database dump via sqlmap.

443.summary: TLS/SSL encrypted web service. Primary objectives: inspect TLS certificate for domain and internal hostname leaks, check for obsolete SSL/TLS protocols and weak ciphers, and audit the web application.

steps.title: Inspect SSL/TLS Certificate for Reconnaissance
steps.desc: Extract Subject Alternative Names (SANs), Common Name (CN), and Issuer to discover associated subdomains and internal domain structure.
steps.indicator: Reveals internal naming convention (e.g. dev-internal.corp.com).

steps.title: Audit SSL/TLS Protocols & Ciphers
steps.desc: Check for deprecated protocols (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1) and historic vulnerabilities (Heartbleed, POODLE, ROBOT).
steps.indicator: Grade C or lower, or acceptance of SSLv3 / TLS 1.0.

steps.title: Web Directory & Vulnerability Audit (HTTPS)
steps.desc: Run content discovery and vulnerability assessment over the encrypted HTTPS connection.
steps.indicator: Accessible administrative panels and sensitive endpoints.

445.summary: Windows file sharing and Active Directory core transport. Primary objectives: check for EternalBlue (MS17-010), enumerate anonymous null shares, list domain users, and check SMB signing.

steps.title: Check for Critical SMB RCE Vulnerabilities (MS17-010 / SMBGhost)
steps.desc: EternalBlue (MS17-010) and SMBGhost (CVE-2020-0796) allow instant SYSTEM-level remote code execution without credentials.
steps.indicator: Reports 'VULNERABLE: Remote Code Execution vulnerability in Microsoft SMBv1'.

steps.title: Enumerate Anonymous Shares (Null Session)
steps.desc: Test if SMB allows unauthenticated listing of network shares and file downloads.
steps.indicator: Read access granted on IPC$, C$, SYSVOL, or departmental backup shares.

steps.title: Enumerate Domain Users, Groups, and Password Policy
steps.desc: Extract Active Directory users, computer names, and lockout threshold policies.
steps.indicator: Dumps valid domain user lists for password spraying.

steps.title: Check SMB Signing (Relay Attack Surface)
steps.desc: If SMB signing is NOT required, attackers can perform NTLM Relay attacks to gain code execution.
steps.indicator: 'message_signing: disabled' or 'signing: False'.

1433.summary: Enterprise database engine. Primary objectives: test default 'sa' administrator credentials, check for unauthenticated access, and verify if xp_cmdshell is enabled for OS command execution.

steps.title: Test Default 'sa' Administrator Credentials
steps.desc: Test common MSSQL administrative logins (sa with blank password, sa:password, sa:sa).
steps.kali_cmd: crackmapexec mssql <target> -u sa -p '' -p 'password' -p 'sa' || hydra -l sa -P passwords.txt mssql://<target>:<port>
steps.indicator: Reports '[+] mssql://sa:... SUCCESS'.

steps.title: Check Database Version & Instance Name
steps.desc: Determine SQL Server edition and patch level.
steps.indicator: Shows instance name and SQL Server build.

steps.title: Test Remote Command Execution via xp_cmdshell
steps.desc: If credentials are valid, check if xp_cmdshell allows executing arbitrary operating system commands.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Use impacket-mssqlclient to enable xp_cmdshell and execute whoami.'
steps.indicator: Successful execution of system commands (e.g. 'nt authority\system').

2049.summary: Unix/Linux remote shared filesystem. Primary objectives: enumerate exported shares (`showmount`), mount the share locally, and check for root privilege escalation (`no_root_squash`).

steps.title: List All Exported Network Shares
steps.desc: Discover which directories are exported and which IP subnets are allowed to access them.
steps.indicator: Returns list of exports (e.g. '/var/www *' or '/home *').

steps.title: Mount Export Locally and Read Files
steps.desc: Attach the remote directory to your local filesystem without requiring passwords.
steps.kali_cmd: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/nfs && sudo mount -t nfs <target>:/exported_dir /mnt/nfs -o nolock
steps.indicator: Access to remote files in /mnt/nfs.

steps.title: Check for no_root_squash Privilege Escalation
steps.desc: If the export is configured with `no_root_squash`, files written as root retain full root SUID ownership.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'If no_root_squash is enabled, upload a setuid root binary to gain root on target.'
steps.indicator: Executing `./rootbash -p` on target provides instant root shell.

2375.summary: Direct access to Docker engine without TLS. CRITICAL RISK: Anyone can interact with Docker to mount the host's root filesystem and gain instant root execution.

steps.title: Verify Unauthenticated Docker API Access
steps.desc: Check if Docker engine answers API requests without client certificates.
steps.indicator: Returns Docker engine version and OS details.

steps.title: List Running Containers and Images
steps.desc: Inspect running containers and proprietary Docker images.
steps.indicator: Returns active container names and exposed ports.

steps.title: Instant Root Command Execution on Host
steps.desc: Spawn a container mounting the host root filesystem (`/`) to gain complete control over the host OS.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Run: docker -H tcp://<target>:<port> run -v /:/host -it alpine chroot /host'
steps.indicator: Root terminal shell on the underlying host operating system.

3306.summary: Popular relational database. Primary objectives: check for default root login without password, enumerate database tables, test for remote access grants, and check UDF code execution.

steps.title: Test Default Root Login (Blank Password)
steps.desc: Test if MySQL root user is configured without a password or with default passwords.
steps.indicator: Direct access to `mysql>` interactive shell prompt.

steps.title: Enumerate Databases and User Accounts
steps.desc: Scan for database schemas, hashes, and configuration details.
steps.indicator: Dumps database names and MySQL password hashes for cracking.

steps.title: Password Spray / Brute Force
steps.desc: Test common administrative credentials against the MySQL database service.
steps.indicator: Hydra discovers valid username and password.

3389.summary: Windows GUI remote management. Primary objectives: check for BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708 RCE), verify Network Level Authentication (NLA) enforcement, and perform credential spraying.

steps.title: Check for BlueKeep Vulnerability (CVE-2019-0708)
steps.desc: BlueKeep allows unauthenticated remote code execution on Windows 7, Server 2008, and XP.
steps.indicator: Reports 'State: VULNERABLE'.

steps.title: Check Network Level Authentication (NLA)
steps.desc: If NLA is disabled, the login screen is displayed publicly, exposing the Windows lock screen and user usernames.
steps.indicator: Dumps internal NetBIOS name, DNS domain name, and Windows OS build.

steps.title: Establish Graphical RDP Session
steps.desc: Connect using FreeRDP or rdesktop to verify credentials or capture screen.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Use an Android RDP app or xfreerdp to connect.'
steps.indicator: Windows desktop interface loads successfully.

5432.summary: Advanced open-source relational database. Primary objectives: test default 'postgres' user credentials, check for unauthenticated network access, and test command execution via COPY FROM PROGRAM.

steps.title: Test Default 'postgres' Account Credentials
steps.desc: Check if default administrative user 'postgres' has a blank password, 'postgres', or 'password'.
steps.kali_cmd: psql -h <target> -p <port> -U postgres || hydra -l postgres -P passwords.txt postgres://<target>:<port>
steps.indicator: Enters `postgres=#` command prompt.

steps.title: Check for Remote Command Execution via COPY FROM PROGRAM
steps.desc: PostgreSQL versions 9.3+ allow superusers to run arbitrary operating system commands.
steps.kali_cmd: psql -h <target> -U postgres -c "CREATE TABLE cmd_exec(cmd_output text); COPY cmd_exec FROM PROGRAM 'whoami'; SELECT * FROM cmd_exec;"
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Run COPY ... FROM PROGRAM in psql to execute OS commands.'
steps.indicator: Returns 'postgres' operating system user.

5900.summary: Cross-platform graphical desktop sharing. Primary objectives: test for VNC Null Authentication bypass, test weak passwords, and connect to view screen.

steps.title: Check for VNC Null Authentication
steps.desc: Many misconfigured VNC servers allow connections with no password specified (Type 1: None).
steps.indicator: Nmap reports 'Authentication types: None'.

steps.title: Brute Force VNC Passwords
steps.desc: VNC passwords are limited to 8 characters and are frequently weak (e.g. password, admin, 12345678).
steps.indicator: Hydra outputs valid 8-character VNC password.

steps.title: Connect to Desktop via VNC Viewer
steps.desc: View and interact with the remote desktop directly.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Use AVNC or bVNC viewer on Android to connect.'
steps.indicator: Remote screen interactive display.

6379.summary: High-performance data store. CRITICAL RISK: Redis defaults to no authentication. If left exposed, attackers can dump memory, inject SSH keys, or schedule cron jobs for root RCE.

steps.title: Test Unauthenticated Access (PING Probe)
steps.desc: Verify if the Redis server accepts commands without an AUTH password.
steps.indicator: Server responds with '+PONG' (CRITICAL: Database is unprotected!).

steps.title: Extract System Info & Dump Database Keys
steps.desc: Extract Redis version, operating system details, and examine cached session keys.
steps.indicator: Dumps system architecture, Redis version, and secret keys.

steps.title: Arbitrary File Write (SSH Authorized Keys / Root RCE)
steps.desc: If Redis is running as root, overwrite /root/.ssh/authorized_keys to achieve direct root SSH access.
steps.kali_cmd: redis-cli -h <target> -p <port> config set dir /root/.ssh/ && redis-cli -h <target> -p <port> config set dbfilename authorized_keys
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Configure dir /root/.ssh/ and dbfilename authorized_keys in redis-cli.'
steps.indicator: Returns '+OK' allowing SSH login as root without password.

8080.service: HTTP Alternate / Tomcat / Jenkins / Spring Boot
8080.summary: Secondary web application server. Primary objectives: check for Apache Tomcat manager, Jenkins Groovy console, and Spring Boot Actuator endpoints.

steps.title: Check for Tomcat Manager Web Interface
steps.desc: Apache Tomcat /manager/html allows uploading WAR packages for instant shell access.
steps.indicator: HTTP 401 with 'WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Tomcat Manager Application"'.

steps.title: Test Default Tomcat Credentials
steps.desc: Test common vendor defaults (tomcat:s3cret, admin:admin, tomcat:tomcat).
steps.indicator: Access to Tomcat Web Application Manager granted.

steps.title: Check for Unauthenticated Jenkins Script Console
steps.desc: Jenkins without security enabled exposes /script, granting arbitrary Groovy system code execution.
steps.indicator: Script console textarea allowing `println "whoami".execute().text`.

steps.title: Check for Spring Boot Actuator Information Leaks
steps.desc: Spring Boot apps often expose sensitive environment variables and passwords at /actuator/env.
steps.indicator: Exposes database passwords, AWS keys, and JWT secrets.

9200.summary: Distributed search database. CRITICAL RISK: Unsecured Elasticsearch instances have caused massive public data breaches. Anyone can query and dump all documents.

steps.title: Verify Unauthenticated Cluster Access
steps.desc: Query the cluster root endpoint to verify authentication status and cluster name.
steps.indicator: Returns cluster name, Lucene version, and tagline 'You Know, for Search'.

steps.title: List All Database Indices and Document Counts
steps.desc: Identify indexes containing customer data, audit logs, or credentials.
steps.indicator: Displays table of indices, doc count, and storage size.

steps.title: Dump Raw Documents from Sensitive Index
steps.desc: Extract documents and records from target indices.
steps.indicator: JSON payload containing user records, PII, and logs.

10000.summary: Web-based Unix management panel. Primary objectives: check for CVE-2019-15107 backdoor in password_change.cgi and test root password brute force.

steps.title: Check for Webmin Backdoor (CVE-2019-15107)
steps.desc: Webmin versions 1.890 through 1.920 contained an unauthenticated root command execution backdoor.
steps.indicator: Outputs 'uid=0(root) gid=0(root)' indicating direct remote code execution.

steps.title: Brute Force Webmin Login
steps.desc: Test common Unix administrative credentials.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Hydra web form brute force for Webmin.'
steps.indicator: Valid session cookie obtained.

27017.summary: NoSQL document database. CRITICAL RISK: Frequently exposed on 0.0.0.0 without authentication. Target for automated ransomware and data extortion.

steps.title: Test Unauthenticated Connection
steps.desc: Check if MongoDB accepts connections without credentials.
steps.indicator: Enters `test>` prompt without prompting for password.

steps.title: List Databases and Collections
steps.desc: Query database names and check for sensitive data.
steps.indicator: Lists database names (e.g. 'users', 'auth', 'customers').

steps.title: Dump Documents from Collection
steps.desc: Read collections and documents.
steps.termux_cmd: echo 'Run mongodump to download all database collections.'
steps.indicator: Successfully dumps BSON records to local disk.
